misconception_description: Student believes that a variable assigned an arithmetic expression containing other variables automatically updates its value when those variables change.

solutions.generated_code:
program PalindromBerikutnya
kamus
  n, kandidat, sisa, hasilBalik : integer
  sudahKetemu : boolean
algoritma
  input(n)
  kandidat <- n + 1
  sisa <- kandidat
  hasilBalik <- 0
  while sisa > 0 do
    hasilBalik <- hasilBalik * 10 + (sisa mod 10)
    sisa <- sisa div 10
  endwhile
  sudahKetemu <- false
  while not sudahKetemu do
    if hasilBalik == kandidat then
      sudahKetemu <- true
    else
      kandidat <- kandidat + 1
    endif
  endwhile
  output(kandidat)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student assigns numstr = str(i) before the loop, genuinely believing that numstr will automatically update whenever the loop variable i changes. From their perspective, numstr is "bound" to the expression str(i), so as i iterates through different values, numstr should reflect the current value of str(i). They use numstr in the palindrome check, confident that it represents the string form of the current loop value. In reality, numstr is fixed at str(num+1) and never updates, causing the code to repeatedly check the same value rather than each successive integer. This will either return num+1 immediately if it happens to be a palindrome, or loop infinitely if it's not.
